questions.stem: How many times do most human cells divide before they die?
questions.why: Most human cells divide 40 to 60 times before dying. Cell division and growth normally occur at roughly the same rate as cell death.

options.t: They divide indefinitely
options.why: Most cells have a finite division limit.

options.t: 10 to 20 times
options.why: That understates the number of divisions.

options.t: 40 to 60 times
100 to 200 times
options.why: That overstates the number of divisions.

questions.stem: What occurs during interphase?
questions.why: Interphase is the in-between, resting stage. The cell takes in nutrients to grow and duplicate, and the product is a cell that has grown and copied its DNA.

options.t: The nucleus divides into two nuclei
options.why: That is telophase.

options.t: The cell specializes into its final form
options.why: That is differentiation.

options.t: Chromosomes line up across the centre
options.why: That is metaphase.

options.t: The cell grows and copies its DNA

questions.stem: Which cells are produced by meiosis rather than mitosis?
questions.why: Meiosis occurs in the production of eggs and sperm. ALL other cells divide by mitosis.

options.t: Red and white blood cells
options.why: Those arise from marrow stem cells by mitosis.

options.t: Eggs (oocytes) and sperm
Skin and liver cells
options.why: Those divide by mitosis.

options.t: Nerve and muscle cells
options.why: Those divide by mitosis if at all.

questions.stem: What is the outcome of meiosis?
questions.why: Meiosis runs two rounds of division, resulting in 4 haploid cells carrying 23 chromosomes — one copy of each paternal and maternal chromosome.

options.t: Two divisions making 2 diploid cells
options.why: Meiosis produces haploid cells.

options.t: One division making 2 diploid cells
options.why: That describes mitosis.

options.t: Two divisions making 4 haploid cells
One division making 4 haploid cells
options.why: Meiosis requires two rounds of division.

questions.stem: What is a diploid cell?
questions.why: Diploid cells carry all 46 chromosomes, 23 from each parent. Mitosis starts with a diploid cell and produces two genetically identical diploid cells.

options.t: A cell holding only 23 chromosomes
options.why: That is a haploid cell.

options.t: A cell that has just finished meiosis
options.why: Meiosis produces haploid cells.

options.t: A cell containing two separate nuclei
options.why: Chromosome count, not nuclei, defines diploid.

options.t: A cell holding all 46 chromosomes

questions.stem: You sustain a laceration and the wound begins to heal with new tissue. Which process is responsible?
questions.why: Mitosis increases cell numbers in the body and handles repair — healing a cut, replacing damaged liver cells, and growth. Growing does not mean cells get bigger; it means there are more of them.

options.t: Mitosis
Differentiation only
options.why: Specialization follows division but does not replace tissue.

options.t: Meiosis
options.why: That produces eggs and sperm only.

options.t: Fermentation
options.why: That is an anaerobic energy pathway.

questions.stem: What is the goal of mitosis?
questions.why: Mitosis produces two genetically identical cells, each with the full 46 chromosomes, from a single parent cell with 46.

options.t: Two cells with half the chromosome count
options.why: The chromosome count is preserved, not halved.

options.t: Two identical cells, each with 46
Two cells differing from the parent cell
options.why: Mitosis produces genetically identical cells.

options.t: Four cells, each holding 23 chromosomes
options.why: That is the outcome of meiosis.

questions.stem: During prophase, what is left behind when the double-stranded chromosomes separate and move to opposite sides of the cell?
questions.why: In prophase the chromosomes are two strands of DNA around a protein. As they separate and move to opposite sides, they leave behind microtubules, which hold structure to the cell.

options.t: Daughter nuclei forming at each pole
options.why: Those form later, in telophase.

options.t: Gap junctions linking the new cells
options.why: Gap junctions are not products of mitosis.

options.t: Microtubules, holding the cell's structure
Chromatin threads left in the nucleus
options.why: Chromatin condenses into chromosomes before this.

questions.stem: Which is the longest phase of mitosis, and what happens during it?
questions.why: Metaphase is the longest phase and can take up to 20 minutes. Chromosomes attach to the microtubules and a motor protein pulls them into line directly across from each other — chromosome migration.

options.t: Prophase — chromosomes condense and pair
options.why: That is an earlier and shorter phase.

options.t: Anaphase — chromosomes are pulled apart
options.why: That is the separation phase.

options.t: Telophase — two new nuclei take shape
options.why: That is the re-forming phase.

options.t: Metaphase — chromosomes line up in rows

questions.stem: What happens during anaphase?
questions.why: Anaphase is separation time. The motor proteins holding the X-shaped chromosome in line begin to pull, snap them apart, and move them outward toward the outer part of the cell.

options.t: The cytoplasm physically splits in two
options.why: That is cleavage.

options.t: Chromosomes line up along the centre
options.why: That is metaphase.

options.t: DNA is copied inside the intact nucleus
options.why: That is interphase.

options.t: Motor proteins snap chromosomes apart

questions.stem: What is cleavage, and what are the resulting cells called?
questions.why: Cleavage is the actual separation — the two new nuclei move apart until they split. The results are called daughter cells, genetic copies of each other and of the parent cell.

options.t: Specialization, making differentiated cells
options.why: That is differentiation.

options.t: DNA duplication, making sister chromatids
options.why: That is interphase.

options.t: Chromosome lineup, making a metaphase plate
options.why: That is metaphase.

options.t: The split itself, making daughter cells

questions.stem: What is differentiation?
questions.why: Differentiation is the specialization of a cell that makes it unique. New cells must be generated for growth and tissue repair to occur.

options.t: Communication between neighbouring cells
options.why: That is cell signaling.

options.t: Physical separation of two daughter cells
options.why: That is cleavage.

options.t: Duplication of the cell's own DNA
options.why: That is interphase.

options.t: Specialization that makes a cell unique

questions.stem: What happens when cell division and growth exceed the rate of cell death?
questions.why: Division and growth normally occur at roughly the same rate as cell death. When division outpaces death, tissues enlarge.

options.t: Differentiation stops
options.why: Differentiation continues alongside growth.

options.t: Tissues enlarge
Tissues atrophy
options.why: That happens when death outpaces division.

options.t: Cells become haploid
options.why: Ploidy is unchanged by growth rate.

questions.stem: What is a tumor, also called a neoplasm?
questions.why: A tumor or neoplasm is a mass of tissue produced by abnormal cell growth and division. It may travel to other organs or tissues — metastasis — to establish secondary tumors.

options.t: A cell that has failed to differentiate
options.why: Failure to differentiate is a feature, not the definition.

options.t: Tissue from abnormal growth and division
A group of cells that stopped dividing
options.why: A tumor is defined by excess division, not arrest.

options.t: A collection of dead cells awaiting removal
options.why: Dead cells are cleared rather than forming a mass.

questions.stem: How do cancer cells grow and multiply?
questions.why: Cancer cells grow and multiply by taking nutrients and space from normal cells — which is why cancer produces wasting even as the tumor grows.

options.t: By dividing without requiring any nutrients
options.why: All cells require nutrients to divide.

options.t: By producing their own independent blood supply from scratch
options.why: They recruit existing vessels rather than creating supply independently.

options.t: By converting normal cells into cancer cells directly
options.why: Cancer arises from mutation, not conversion of neighbours.

options.t: By taking nutrients and space from normal cells

questions.stem: What is cell signaling?
questions.why: Cell signaling is electrochemical communication between cells. Cells must communicate both with other cells and within themselves in order to work as a cohesive unit.

options.t: Transfer of DNA from parent to daughter
options.why: That is cell division.

options.t: Transport of nutrients across the membrane
options.why: That is membrane transport.

options.t: Electrochemical communication between cells
Specialization occurring during development
options.why: That is differentiation.

questions.stem: Cell signaling is used to accomplish which of the following?
questions.why: Signaling maintains homeostasis, fights infection, drives reproduction, and supports normal function. Alterations in those signals can lead to dysfunction.

options.t: DNA replication ahead of cell division
options.why: That occurs during interphase.

options.t: ATP production inside the mitochondria
options.why: That is a mitochondrial function.

options.t: Homeostasis, defense, and reproduction
Surface area increase for absorption
options.why: That is the microvilli's role.

questions.stem: Match each phase of mitosis to what happens during it.
questions.why: Replicate, separate, line up, snap apart, re-form, split. Metaphase is the longest phase; cleavage is the only step that physically divides the cell.
pairs: Two copies are made of every DNA strand inside the nucleus
Double-stranded chromosomes separate toward opposite sides, leaving microtubules
Chromosomes attach to microtubules and are pulled into line across from each other
Motor proteins snap the chromosomes apart and move them outward
Two genetic parts begin forming into new cells
The two new nuclei move apart until they split into daughter cells

questions.stem: Match each stage of energy production to its location or yield.
questions.why: Glycolysis is cytoplasmic and anaerobic; everything after pyruvate oxidation needs oxygen and happens inside the mitochondria. Fermentation is the backup when oxygen runs short.
pairs: Occurs in the cytoplasm; nets 2 ATP, 2 pyruvates, 2 NADH
Removes one carbon from pyruvate to form acetyl CoA
Occurs in the mitochondrial matrix; yields 2 CO2, 2 ATP, 6 NADH
Anaerobic pathway using NADH; produces lactic acid in humans
